formNote: The Shuowen: 易，蜥易 … 象形 — “a lizard (the chameleon?); a pictograph”, and adds 祕書說：日月為易，象陰陽也, “the occult books say sun and moon make 易, picturing yin and yang.” Mojidata IDS gives ⿱日勿: the lower part is 勿, not 月.
summary: Change, and the Book of Changes: the Yijing’s sixty-four hexagrams model a world that never stops turning. 易 also means easy, and commentators made three meanings of it: the simple, the changing and the unchanging.
placement: Below the centre on the left, between the lower lobes, beside 時: change, with time. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: A Lizard, or Sun and Moon
satellites.evidence: The Shuowen gives two readings of the graph: a lizard, the creature that changes colour, and, from the occult books, 日月為易, “sun and moon make 易”, picturing yin and yang.
satellites.caveat: Mojidata IDS analyses the modern graph as 日 over 勿, not 月; the sun-and-moon reading is the Shuowen’s report, not the graph’s structure.

satellites.title: Generating Generation
satellites.evidence: The Xici: 生生之謂易 — “generation upon generation: that is called change.” Change is not decay but the continuing production of life.
